title: Introduce yourself and understand another person
lessons:
# Chapter 2 — Introduce yourself and understand another person

## Goals and prerequisites
Use Chapter 1's greetings and sound-decoding routine to exchange names, origins, languages, work, and contact details. If the alphabet sounds and polite chunks are still new, review those first; you do not need to master them before continuing. By the end, you can give a short introduction, recognize common subject pronouns, and use present forms of **être** and **avoir** in high-frequency expressions.

## Subject pronouns and two essential verbs
French normally states the subject: `je` (I), `tu` (you, singular informal), `il` (he/it), `elle` (she/it), `on` (one/we in conversation), `nous` (we), `vous` (you formal or plural), `ils` (they, masculine or mixed), and `elles` (they, all feminine). Use **vous** with a stranger or in a formal service encounter. In speech, **on** is often more common than **nous** for “we.” The final written letters in many verb forms are silent, so listen for the whole subject-plus-verb chunk.

`Être` (to be): je suis, tu es, il/elle/on est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont. Examples: `Je suis canadienne` (I am Canadian; feminine speaker) and `Vous êtes étudiant ?` (Are you a student?). `Avoir` (to have): j'ai, tu as, il/elle/on a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont. Its common contractions are `j'ai` and, in speech, linked forms such as `vous avez`. French uses avoir in many age and condition expressions: `J'ai trente ans` (I am thirty years old), `J'ai faim` (I am hungry).

## Identity language
To state a name, say `Je m'appelle Samira` (My name is Samira). To ask, use `Comment vous appelez-vous ?` (What is your name? formal) or the more conversational `Vous vous appelez comment ?` Origins use `Je viens de...` (I come from...) or `J'habite à...` (I live in...). With country names, prepositions vary by country: `au Canada`, `en France`, `aux États-Unis`; learn the location with its preposition as a chunk. For a first introduction, a city is simpler and avoids guessing the country form.

A basic occupation can follow être: `Je suis infirmier` (I am a nurse; masculine form). Many job nouns have gendered forms; use a form you know, or give a neutral detail such as your field of work. Nationality adjectives agree with the person in writing: `canadien` / `canadienne`. In speech, these forms may sound similar or different depending on the word, so do not guess spelling from sound alone.

## Speak, listen, read, write
Listen for facts rather than trying to translate every word: name, city, language, job, and one contact detail. In a short self-introduction, two or three facts plus a follow-up question are better than a memorized list. For writing, use line breaks or simple connectors (`et`, and; `mais`, but). Read a short profile and verify each fact against the text.

## Cumulative retrieval
Attempt each answer before revealing it; say the answer aloud and then add one true detail about yourself.

Before the first reveal: From memory, give the je forms of être and avoir, say which verb French uses for age, and name the formal/plural word for “you.”

:::answer
`Je suis` = I am; `j'ai` = I have. Say age with avoir: `J'ai vingt-neuf ans` = I am twenty-nine years old. Formal/plural “you” is `vous`.
:::

Before the second reveal: Without looking, give a short French introduction with a name, a city, and a language you speak; connect two facts with et.

:::answer
A short introduction can be: `Bonjour, je m'appelle Lina. J'habite à Ottawa et je parle anglais.` = Hello, my name is Lina. I live in Ottawa and speak English.
:::

## Check and space your review
Can you introduce yourself for 20–30 seconds without reading? Can you hear a name and city in a short message? Can you choose between être and avoir for an identity versus age? Mark uncertain forms in an error log. Retrieve 10–15 items today, repeat missed items tomorrow, after three days, and after seven days. On review, change one personal detail to a new truthful detail so the phrase stays flexible rather than becoming a fixed recital.

bank.prompt: Give your name using the standard chunk.
bank.cue: The verb literally means I call myself.
The question word comes at the end.

bank.prompt: Translate the speaker's place of origin.
Say where you live using a city.
Give an origin with venir de.

bank.cue: The job follows être without an article.
En réunion is a location/state phrase.

bank.prompt: Ask a friend whether they are local.

bank.cue: Place ne and pas around suis.

bank.prompt: Introduce yourself as new to the area.
bank.cue: Nouvelle agrees with a feminine speaker.

bank.prompt: Identify the family member and job.

bank.en: My sister works at the hospital.

bank.cue: The verb ends in -ons for nous.
Two language names are joined by et.
The verb comes before the subject.

bank.fr: Je parle espagnol à la maison.
bank.cue: À la maison means at home.

bank.prompt: Hear how many languages the friend speaks.

bank.cue: Put un peu before the language.
The noun at the end means question.

bank.prompt: Respond that the message is clear.

bank.fr: Je ne comprends pas votre nom.
Quel est votre nom de famille ?
Mon nom de famille est Roy.
bank.prompt: Give a surname using the full expression.
bank.cue: Nom de famille is one phrase.

bank.fr: Mon adresse est sur le formulaire.
bank.en: My address is on the form.

bank.prompt: Locate her home relative to a landmark.
bank.cue: Près de becomes près du before masculine du.

bank.fr: Ils habitent dans le même immeuble.
bank.en: They live in the same building.

bank.fr: Nous habitons sur la rue King.

bank.cue: French literally says I have years.

bank.en: My son is eight years old.
bank.cue: The age belongs to the son.

bank.en: My daughter is eleven years old.
bank.cue: Onze begins with a vowel sound.

bank.prompt: Make this statement negative and change the article as needed.
bank.cue: After ne...pas, des changes to de.

bank.prompt: Identify what the speaker asks about.
bank.cue: Animal can mean pet in this context.

bank.fr: Elle a un chien très calme.
bank.en: She has a very calm dog.

bank.cue: The adjective ends in a silent t.
Médecin has the same written form for both genders.

bank.en: My parents are in Quebec City.

bank.cue: Célibataire does not change for gender.

bank.fr: Nous sommes quatre à la maison.
bank.en: There are four of us at home.
bank.prompt: Understand how many people live there.

bank.fr: Il y a cinq personnes dans ma famille.
bank.en: There are five people in my family.
bank.prompt: Describe your family size with il y a.

bank.cue: The spelling adds e for a feminine subject.

bank.en: My birthday falls on a Monday.
bank.cue: Tomber un jour means to fall on a day.

bank.fr: Je suis libre après le travail.
bank.prompt: Understand when the person is free.

bank.en: He is on a business trip.
I am responsible for the project.
bank.prompt: Describe your role on a project.
bank.cue: Responsable is the same for all genders.

bank.fr: Je suis en formation cette semaine.
Mon cours commence à neuf heures.
bank.en: My class starts at nine o'clock.

bank.cue: Électronique distinguishes it from a postal address.

bank.fr: Mon numéro de téléphone est facile à retenir.
bank.en: My phone number is easy to remember.
bank.prompt: Say whether a phone number is easy to remember.
Confirm you are recording someone's address.

bank.fr: Mon courriel est sur la fiche.
bank.en: My email is on the form.

bank.cue: Mon agrees with famille's grammatical gender.
Présenter is used to introduce a person.
The feminine speaker's spelling is shown.

bank.en: We have known each other for a long time.
bank.cue: Depuis longtemps means for a long time.

bank.prompt: Say you know an area well.
bank.cue: Connaître is used with a place/person.
Tous ses voisins is the object.
Patients is masculine or mixed plural.
French says I have a lot of luck.
Avoir tort is the opposite of avoir raison.

bank.en: I have an appointment with my adviser.
bank.prompt: Mention an appointment and its person.
bank.cue: Avoir rendez-vous is a fixed chunk.

bank.fr: Je suis contente de vous rencontrer.

activities.title: Meet a new colleague
activities.prompt: Listen for the speaker's name, city, and job. Choose the job.
activities.script: Bonjour, je m'appelle Farid. J'habite à Gatineau depuis deux ans et je travaille dans une clinique. Je suis infirmier. Et vous, vous travaillez dans quel domaine ?
activities.explanation: The speaker says, « Je suis infirmier »; he works as a nurse.

activities.title: A family introduction
activities.prompt: Listen to the connected introduction. How many children are mentioned?
activities.script: Je vous présente ma famille. Mon fils a huit ans et ma fille a onze ans. Nous habitons dans le même quartier que mes parents, à Québec.
activities.explanation: The speaker names a son and a daughter: two children.

activities.title: Read a staff profile
activities.prompt: Read the short profile. Which language does the person study?
activities.passage: Profil de Nadia : Je m'appelle Nadia. Je suis originaire de Tunis et j'habite maintenant à Ottawa. Je travaille dans un bureau et j'apprends le français en ligne.
activities.explanation: The last clause says she is learning French online.

activities.title: Understand an appointment card
activities.prompt: Read the card and identify the appointment time.
activities.passage: Centre médical du Parc — Patient : Louis Roy. Rendez-vous avec la docteure Benali, jeudi à 10 h 30. Veuillez arriver dix minutes avant.
activities.explanation: The card lists Thursday at 10:30; it separately asks the patient to arrive ten minutes early.

activities.title: Introduce yourself and ask back
activities.prompt: Give a 30-second introduction with your name, where you live, one language you speak, and one work or study detail. Finish by asking your listener one polite question.
activities.model: Bonjour, je m'appelle Maya. J'habite à Toronto et je parle anglais. J'étudie le français le soir. Et vous, quel est votre prénom ?
rubric: I included at least three personal facts.
I used a subject pronoun with a suitable present-tense form.
I asked a relevant question and spoke in short, clear groups.

activities.title: Write a profile for a class
activities.prompt: Write a 35–55-word introduction for a French class message board. Include your name, city, languages, work or studies, and one friendly question to classmates.
activities.model: Bonjour tout le monde ! Je m'appelle Samir et j'habite à Halifax. Je travaille dans un bureau et j'apprends le français depuis quelques mois. Je parle arabe et anglais. J'aime rencontrer des gens. Vous étudiez le français depuis longtemps ?
rubric: The profile includes name, place, languages, and work/study.
Present forms of être, avoir, or regular verbs communicate clear facts.
A final question invites a response; the register suits a class forum.
